The main column splits items by what happened to them. An Unfulfilled card lists what’s left to ship, worked out as purchased minus fulfilled minus refunded. Each shipment gets its own card with carrier, tracking link, delivery status and items, and refunded items get a Refunded card. The Payment card shows the total and only the lines that matter right now (refunded and net, an authorization with its expiry, or a balance due); subtotal, discounts, shipping, tax and currency conversion sit behind Breakdown. It has Capture payment for authorizations and Send invoice for pending or failed payments.

The timeline reads like Shopify, Linear and Stripe activity feeds: a rail with one icon per event type (status color only on the icon), a short title built from the order data (“Payment of $564.41 captured”, “Shipped with UPS” with the tracking number linked), a muted second line and a relative time with the exact date in a tooltip. Day labels stick while you scroll. Customer emails fold into the event that sent them (“Customer emailed”, with Resend in Show details), three or more same-kind events in a row collapse into one line, and older history folds behind “Show N earlier events”. Comments are cards with avatar, author, edit and delete, and attachments as chips. Filter by All, Comments or System. The composer is one line until you focus it, then shows attachments, “Only visible to staff” and Post (⌘↵), and posts optimistically with retry. The right rail keeps to what matters: notes and tags only appear when they have content or can be edited, the customer card drops repeated name and phone lines, and conversion and risk show a one-line summary with details behind Show more. Cancelled, on hold, archived and loading states, and actions a staff member isn’t allowed to take, are all handled with a reason.
